correctness.rationale: The Freshman-dream identity produces the irreducible primitive polynomial xa³−zb³. Its four partial derivatives are a³,−b³,0,0, giving a complete intersection of degree nine. The four basepoint-free sections define a finite birational map from P(O(3)⊕O(1))=F2, with an isomorphism off the singular line and Frobenius on its preimage; smoothness gives normalization and geometric injectivity gives a universal homeomorphism. Projective-bundle point counts then prove the zeta formula. Exact symbolic/F3/F9 checker ran successfully.

value.rationale: The naïve reduction and known good reduction of a distinguished complex 64-line quartic have genuinely different geometry; the naive fibre is a nonnormal rational surface obtained by a degree-three Frobenius pinch. Determining its complete scheme-theoretic singular support, finite normalization, and zeta function supplies coherent geometric/arithmetic structure at the exceptional prime, not a renamed polynomial or an arbitrary finite census.
